record.original_question: Given a general k-orbit polytope together with a distinguished generating set for its automorphism group, describe a construction that rebuilds the polytope as a coset geometry of that group, in the same spirit that regular and chiral polytopes can be reconstructed from suitable generator data.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Describe a way to build a general polytope as a coset geometry of its automorphism group, given a distinguished set of generators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) are graded by rank from -1 to n, in which every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G are faces with ranks differing by 2, there are exactly two faces strictly between F and G. The automorphism group Aut(P) acts freely on flags; P is called a k-orbit polytope if this action has exactly k orbits on flags. For a regular polytope (k=1), fixing a base flag Φ yields distinguished involutory generators ρ_0,...,ρ_{n-1} of Aut(P), and P can be reconstructed as the coset geometry on Aut(P) with respect to the parabolic subgroups generated by all ρ_i except one. An analogous coset-geometry reconstruction is known for chiral polytopes (a class of 2-orbit polytopes).

Problem. Let P be an arbitrary k-orbit abstract polytope (k ≥ 1) and let Γ = Aut(P) be equipped with a distinguished set of generators arising from the flag-orbit structure of P. Provide a general construction that recovers P as a coset geometry of Γ from this generator data alone, giving necessary and sufficient conditions (on the generators and on intersections of certain subgroups) under which an abstractly given group with such a generating set arises as the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope reconstructable from those generators.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 paper by Hubard and Schulte ("All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes") provides a general coset-geometry reconstruction of any abstract polytope from its automorphism group together with a distinguished generating set, and characterizes such groups by generator/intersection conditions. Specific small cases (k = 2 chiral, k = 3 polyhedra) have explicit detailed treatments. Hence the problem is largely resolved in general, though sharper case-by-case characterizations for higher k continue to be studied.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes and shows all such polytopes can be built as coset geometries.
status_evidence.claim: A general coset-geometry construction for k-orbit polytopes from generators of the automorphism group has been given.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions on generators of Γ to construct a 3-orbit polyhedron with Γ as automorphism group.
status_evidence.claim: The k=3 polyhedral case has an explicit generator-based reconstruction.
